subject: Daily AcreetionOS Update -- November 22, 2026
body:
Daily AcreetionOS Update - November 22, 2026

Good morning from Spokane! The AcreetionOS team is wrapping up another productive week with several polished improvements landing across our repositories. Natalie and Darren have been busy squashing edge-case bugs and tightening up the deployment pipeline for a smoother user experience.

On the development front, a pair of CSP fixes went live to address Cloudflare edge caching issues that caused pre-deploy 404 errors for page-status.js and consent-init.js. These cache-busting references ensure visitors always load the latest scripts without stale content getting stuck at the CDN layer.

The AcreetionOS-Xlibre desktop environment received a welcome usability fix — bottom bar icons are now properly clickable again after a regression slipped through. Darren also updated the Electron runtime to the latest version, bringing security patches and performance improvements for new users spinning up the installer.

Our wallpaper collection got its own dedicated repository with acreetionos-wallpapers, complete with submodule tracking back to our GitLab instance for seamless asset management. The initial commit lays the groundwork for curated background packs that will ship with future ISO releases.

The blog deployment pipeline was refined with a new build configuration targeting blog.acreetionos.org, ensuring GitHub Pages picks up the correct site context. This streamlines content updates and keeps the news feed fresh without manual intervention.

In broader community news, the LLVM project announced the conclusion of its relicensing effort — a significant milestone for compiler infrastructure that underpins much of our toolchain. The transition to a more permissive license model aligns well with our repository sovereignty principles.

Vim Classic 8.3.1 dropped this week with stability fixes and compatibility improvements for the beloved modal editor. Many of our users rely on Vim for configuration work, and this maintenance release keeps the classic experience solid on modern systems.

Security updates rolled out Friday from AlmaLinux covering bind9.18, bubblewrap, fence-agents, freerdp, grafana, and several Java and GStreamer components. While AcreetionOS draws from Arch upstream, monitoring downstream enterprise patches helps us anticipate upstream fixes.

Tip of the day: if you're customizing your Cinnamon panel and icons stop responding, a quick `cinnamon --replace` from Alt+F2 often resolves it without a full logout. We're documenting more of these workflow shortcuts on the wiki for the 1.1 release cycle.
